voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: There is a valley in Norway that the locals call the Valley of Death.
In nineteen seventy, a woman was found there, burned alive — fifty sleeping pills inside her, and her jewelry laid out on the rock beside her.
Every label had been cut from her clothes. Every maker's mark scrubbed away. The name scraped off her own skin cream.
She had travelled under at least eight false names, and kept her own movements written in code.
Fifty years and a full strand of her DNA later, they still cannot tell you who she was.
The full story is on the channel.
